title: The Middle East's coalitions of convenience
gist: The authors argue the Turkey-Saudi-Pakistan Mecca Joint Defence Agreement is not a new 'Arab NATO' (neither partner aided Riyadh when Houthis struck its East-West pipeline and seized Mokha) but may work as one node in a web of narrow, overlapping coalitions, alongside Saudi Arabia's new 14-country Red Sea maritime alliance. Grand regional alliances like CENTO and the GCC have repeatedly failed on divergent threat perceptions.

insights.claim: Saudi Arabia's 'Article 5 moment' came when the Houthis struck its East-West oil pipeline and then took Mokha, which controls access to the Bab el-Mandeb, yet neither Pakistan nor Turkey came to its aid.
insights.speaker: Ibrahim Al-Marashi and Tanya Goudsouzian
insights.so_what: Saudi export infrastructure and Red Sea chokepoints are exposed, and the new pact did not deter attacks: oil and shipping risk premium.
insights.quote: Neither Pakistan nor Turkey came to Saudi Arabia’s aid, although both have since offered words of support.
insights.locator: The announcement of the Mecca Joint Defence

insights.claim: Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia face different strategic problems (Greece, the eastern Mediterranean and Israel; India; and Iran plus the UAE respectively), so military cooperation alone will not make the Mecca Agreement durable.
insights.speaker: Ibrahim Al-Marashi and Tanya Goudsouzian
insights.so_what: Do not price the pact as a credible mutual-defence guarantee for Gulf assets.
insights.quote: Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia are not responding to the same strategic problem.

insights.claim: At their first committee meeting in Istanbul on 31 August 2026, the Mecca signatories agreed to a permanent secretariat in Saudi Arabia and deeper defence cooperation.
insights.speaker: Ibrahim Al-Marashi and Tanya Goudsouzian
insights.so_what: Early institutionalisation is a signpost to watch for whether the pact becomes real.

insights.claim: The Mecca Agreement would only become significant with genuine intelligence sharing, joint exercises, interoperable forces, agreed attack responses and dispute-resolution mechanisms.
insights.speaker: Ibrahim Al-Marashi and Tanya Goudsouzian
insights.so_what: Provides concrete milestones to track the pact's real deterrent value.
insights.locator: The Mecca Agreement could become significant

insights.claim: Unlike CENTO, the Mecca Agreement is a regional initiative not sponsored by a Western power, reflecting its members' bad experiences of over-reliance on outside powers.
insights.speaker: Ibrahim Al-Marashi and Tanya Goudsouzian
insights.so_what: Signals declining US centrality in Gulf security and a push for strategic autonomy.

themes.theme: Overlapping narrow coalitions as the new security model

insights.claim: The future of Middle East security may belong to a network of overlapping coalitions, each built around a narrow set of threats, rather than a grand regional alliance.
insights.speaker: Ibrahim Al-Marashi and Tanya Goudsouzian
insights.so_what: Expect fragmented, issue-specific alignments; analyse risk per coalition rather than as bloc vs bloc.
insights.quote: The future of the Middle East may belong not to a grand regional alliance but a network of overlapping coalitions

insights.claim: In August 2026 Riyadh helped establish a 14-country Multinational Maritime Defence Alliance to protect shipping through the Red Sea, Bab el-Mandeb and Gulf of Aden, including Egypt, Pakistan and Turkey but excluding the UAE and Oman.
insights.speaker: Ibrahim Al-Marashi and Tanya Goudsouzian
insights.so_what: A regional naval effort to secure Red Sea shipping lanes could affect freight and insurance rates; the UAE's exclusion signals Saudi-Emirati rifts.
insights.locator: Saudi Arabia is making a parallel effort

insights.claim: Where Washington once deterred the Houthis with airstrikes, Riyadh now seeks a collective maritime security network instead of relying on a single external power.
insights.speaker: Ibrahim Al-Marashi and Tanya Goudsouzian
insights.so_what: Reduced US deterrence capacity in the Red Sea raises the baseline for shipping disruption risk.
insights.quote: Where Washington once had the capacity to deter the Houthis through airstrikes
insights.locator: Saudi Arabia is making a parallel effort

insights.claim: Egypt declined the Mecca Agreement but joined the maritime alliance, while Pakistan and Turkey joined both, showing states joining multiple purpose-specific arrangements.
insights.speaker: Ibrahim Al-Marashi and Tanya Goudsouzian
insights.so_what: Alignment is transactional and issue-specific, making regional alignments more fluid.

insights.claim: An all-encompassing regional security framework is likely a non-starter because the region's interests are too diverse and threats too varied; smaller coalitions are less ambitious but more realistic.
insights.speaker: Ibrahim Al-Marashi and Tanya Goudsouzian
insights.so_what: Skepticism toward 'Arab NATO' headlines is warranted.
insights.quote: Smaller coalitions may be less ambitious, but they may also be more realistic.
insights.locator: Critics will ask whether the region

insights.claim: A security alliance cannot merely assemble power against a common threat; members must agree whose security is protected, what interests they share and what they will do for each other.
insights.speaker: Ibrahim Al-Marashi and Tanya Goudsouzian
insights.so_what: A test for judging any new security pact's durability.
insights.locator: The pact, later known as CENTO

insights.claim: The 1955 Baghdad Pact (CENTO) unravelled through nationalism, competing ambitions and revolutions, losing Iraq in 1958 and dissolving in 1979 after the Shah's fall.
insights.speaker: Ibrahim Al-Marashi and Tanya Goudsouzian
insights.so_what: Historical base rate for Western-modelled regional alliances is poor.

insights.claim: The GCC, despite existing since 1981, has repeatedly pursued competing foreign policies and is close to institutional paralysis; it has yet to respond coherently to Israel's assaults in the ongoing Iran war despite meeting after the Qatar attacks.
insights.speaker: Ibrahim Al-Marashi and Tanya Goudsouzian
insights.so_what: Gulf states will respond divergently to shocks; do not treat GCC as a unified bloc.
insights.quote: the GCC has yet to respond coherently to Israel’s assaults

insights.claim: Unlike Europe, where coal and steel built interdependence, GCC members are rentier states whose economic integration has not erased competition over energy, trade and regional influence.
insights.speaker: Ibrahim Al-Marashi and Tanya Goudsouzian
insights.so_what: Gulf economic competition (energy, trade hubs) will persist and shape policy divergence.
insights.locator: In the Gulf, where one might expect

insights.claim: NATO endured largely because two devastating wars made pursuing national interests through war intolerable; the 2026 war, though the most region-wide yet, has not produced similar convergence.
insights.speaker: Ibrahim Al-Marashi and Tanya Goudsouzian
insights.so_what: Absent a unifying catastrophe, expect continued fragmentation and conflict risk in the Middle East.
insights.quote: none has affected the entire region as much as the 2026 war

insights.claim: Nasser rejected CENTO and played the US and USSR against each other, extracting concessions from both, which brought Soviet arms into Egypt.
insights.speaker: Ibrahim Al-Marashi and Tanya Goudsouzian
insights.so_what: Hedging between great powers is a long-standing regional strategy, echoed in today's strategic-autonomy push.
